title: Tor-independence for monoid-ideal quotients in a log regular chart
statement: Let $(X,M,\alpha)$ be a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $\bar x$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and let $A=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$ be its strict henselization [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Put $P=\overline M_{\bar x}$. Suppose a chart $c:P\to M|_W$ is given on a pointed etale neighbourhood $(W,\bar w)\to(X,\bar x)$ [def-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods], and its induced map $P\to\overline M_{\bar w}=\overline M_{\bar x}$ is the chosen identification. Let $a:P\to(A,\cdot)$ be the composite of this chart with the structural map and the map to the geometric stalk. A monoid ideal means a subset $I\subseteq P$ with $I+P\subseteq I$, allowing $I=\varnothing$. For every monoid ideal $I$, writing $R=\mathbf Z[P]$, $IR$ for the ideal of $R$ generated by the monomials from $I$, and letting $R\to A$ be induced by $a$, one has$$\operatorname{Tor}^{R}_1(R/IR,A)=0.$$Here Tor is the module Tor functor of [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules].

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.4.3 proof, invoking Kato (1994), 6.1(ii), for Tor-independence of monoid-ideal quotients with the structure ring.

proof.text: The sharp-chart lemma gives that $P$ is sharp fs. Apply the completed-chart lemma to the given chart, obtaining a replacement characteristic chart $a'$ and $n\ge0$ with $\widehat A=B_k(P,n)$ in equal characteristic, or $\widehat A=B_C(P,n)/(\theta)$ with $\theta-p\in J=(z^q\ (q\ne0),t_i)$ in mixed characteristic, compatibly with $a'(q)=z^q$. Keep the $R$-action through $a'$ until the final step.

source.place: VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p.70; VIII 3.4.3, printed p.110.

proof.text: Choose a Noetherian affine open $\operatorname{Spec}D$ around $x$ using local Noetherianity. The affine-stalk localization and localization-Noetherianity statements make $\mathcal O_{X,x}=D_{\mathfrak p}$ Noetherian. The affine strict-local comparison identifies $A$ locally with its algebraic strict henselization relative to the separable closure of $\kappa(x)$ in the geometric-point field; it also says $A$ is strictly henselian. The index pairs $(S,\chi:S\to K)$ of that algebraic strict henselization are the triples $(S,\ker\chi,\kappa(\ker\chi)\to K)$ over the closed point, with the same morphisms, so it is the strict henselization of the triples statement used by the completion theorem. A local isomorphism identifies maximal ideals and every quotient by their powers, hence completions. The strict-henselization completion theorem therefore gives the faithfully flat map $A\to\widehat A$.

source.place: VIII 3.4.3 completion reduction; algebraic strict-henselization comparison and faithfully flat completion as in retained Step 2.

proof.text: In equal characteristic the completed-monomial tensor lemma with $L=k$ makes $IR\otimes_R\widehat A\to\widehat A$ injective. In mixed characteristic apply it with $L=C$ to $B_0=B_C(P,n)$, identifying $H=IR\otimes_RB_0$ with $IB_0\subseteq B_0$. The Cohen-quotient lemma makes $\theta$ injective on $B_0/IB_0$. Thus $H\cap\theta B_0=\theta H$: if $h=\theta b\in H$, regularity on the quotient gives $b\in H$. Consequently $H/\theta H\to B_0/(\theta)$ is injective. The maps $[x\otimes b]\leftrightarrow x\otimes[b]$ identify $H/\theta H$ with $IR\otimes_R(B_0/(\theta))$ by the tensor relations, so the required multiplication is injective in both models.

source.place: VI 1.6 models and VIII 3.4.3; retained Steps 3 and 4, with the reduction argument explicitly on elements.

proof.text: Tor symmetry followed by the ideal-kernel statement (a) identifies $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(R/IR,\widehat A)$ with $\ker(IR\otimes_R\widehat A\to\widehat A)=0$. Faithfully flat coefficient base change descends this to $\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(R/IR,A_{a'})=0$. For the original chart, $a(q)\in A^\times$ forces the image of $q$ in $\overline M_{\bar x}=M_{\bar x}/A^\times$ to be $0$, and $P\to\overline M_{\bar x}$ is the bijective chosen identification, so $q=0$. Apply the chart face-Tor comparison to the original sharp chart, with $F=\{0\}$, $P_F=P$, $P_x=P$, section $s=\mathrm{id}$, and $b=a'$. Both characteristic maps are the specified identification. Its Tor isomorphism gives vanishing for the original action $a$, as required.

source.place: VIII 3.4.3; retained Steps 5--6 and the existing face-Tor comparison specialized to a sharp chart.
